topic: Cyclic sighing: animated explainer (Balban et al., 2023)
caption:
Cyclic sighing: a five-minute breathing pattern with two breaths in and one long breath out.

In a Stanford study, people practised one of three breathing patterns or mindfulness meditation for five minutes a day over a month. Every group reported feeling a little calmer after each session. Cyclic sighing, with its double inhale and long exhale, showed the biggest lift in positive mood compared with meditation.

How to try it: breathe in through your nose, take one more small sip of air on top, then breathe out slowly through your mouth. Repeat for up to five minutes. If you feel light-headed, go back to breathing normally.

You can practise cyclic sighing with the free guided breathing in our Tools and Courses app. Find it in our profile links.

Worth knowing: this was one small study, mostly with university students, and it was registered after it began. Treat it as something to explore, not a promise.

Save this for later.

Research: Balban, M. Y., Neri, E., Kogon, M. M., Weed, L., Nouriani, B., Jo, B., Holl, G., Zeitzer, J. M., Spiegel, D., & Huberman, A. D. (2023). Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal. Cell Reports Medicine, 4(1), 100895. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2022.100895
